data.long_meaning: In biblical times, palms were symbols of victory and triumph. Palm branches were used to welcome kings and prophets, such as Jesus during His triumphal entry into Jerusalem (Matthew 21:8). The name Palm carries the meaning “Hand or branch” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Palm usually hope their child will grow to embody hand or branch and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes victory, triumph, and divine welcome.
data.etymology: Palm belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Hand or branch.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Palm total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: In Christian tradition, the celebration of Palm Sunday marks the commencement of Holy Week leading to the crucifixion and resurrection of Jesus. During this day, palm leaves or branches are blessed and processed in churches and the homes of believers.
data.spiritual_significance: Symbolizing Christ’s humility, the use of palm leaves as a part of the Palm Sunday celebrations serves as a reminder of Jesus' entry into Jerusalem riding on a donkey, emphasizing His meekness, peace, and power despite the political expectations of His people. The palms also represent the spiritual victory Christians experience through their faith in Jesus, as well as the promise of Palm Sunday: the assurance that how things may appear in the present (Jesus entering Jerusalem as a humble king), ultimately leads to redemption and resurrection.
